battle.name: 捻軍起義
battle.theater: 皖北蘇北豫東魯西四省交界
battle.brief: 一八五三年春，張樂行在安徽亳州雉河集大集各旗，與太平天國互聯，北方抗清武裝連成一體；其後捻軍獨自經營皖北、蘇北、豫東的圩寨與騎兵游擊，至一八六八年夏季被清廷以蒙古騎兵、淮軍洋槍與壕溝封鎖合圍而平定。本卡線膛砲即清方攻寨時壓制寨牆與騎兵的核心火力。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 捻軍起義的一方，是起自安徽亳州、蒙城一帶的「捻黨」武裝。捻黨在河南、山東、蘇北、皖北傳流數十年，咸豐初年因太平天國起義而由秘密結社轉為公開武裝，按大旗分股，首領稱捻首，每旗人數自數千至數萬不等，股與股之間並無統一指揮，內部又分老捻與新捻，配備與作戰風格差異很大。張樂行一八五一年在蒙城起義，次年攻取雉河集作為根據地；一八五三年太平天國定都南京後，捻軍首領在雉河集大集各旗與太平軍互通款曲，張樂行受封爵位，捻軍一度被置於太平軍北伐與西征的體系之內充當北方機動力量。太平天國覆亡之後捻軍完全脫離，成為北方獨立的武裝，一八六〇年代其勢力遍及皖北、蘇北、豫東、魯西四省交界的廣大鄉村。交戰的另一方是清廷及其地方軍力：中樞由軍機處與戶部調度軍餉，戰區由河道總督、兩江總督、直隸總督與河南、山東、安徽各巡撫分節制，綠營與旗營守城，團練與練勇守鄉，勇營作攻勢作戰。一八五五年起僧格林沁率領察哈爾蒙古騎兵充當追擊主力；一八六〇年代起，曾國藩、李鴻章麾下的楚勇與淮軍配上上海購得的洋槍與線膛砲，成為攻堅主力，李鴻章更以運河漕船輸送糧械。地方團練、寨堡與民夫構成縱深，運河沿線的糧臺與漕運是清軍補給的命脈。兩陣營的界線並非單純的官民之別：多數捻眾原為被抽丁、抽糧、迫稅的農民、運河船丁與流民，戰局之中亦屢有地方團練與散兵改旗易幟，倒向捻軍一方。
countriesEn: The side of the Nian rising was the armed body of the Nian societies that grew up around Bozhou and Mengcheng in Anhui. These societies had circulated across Henan, Shandong, northern Jiangsu and northern Anhui for decades; in the early Xianfeng years, pushed by the Taiping rebellion, they turned from hidden cells into open bands, organised in great banners, each banner led by a Nian chief and numbering from several thousand to tens of thousands. There was no common command between one banner and the next, and inside the movement old Nian and new Nian differed sharply in equipment and in style of fighting. Zhang Lexing rose at Mengcheng in 1851 and took Zhiheji the next year as his base; after the Taiping settled their capital at Nanjing in 1853 the Nian chiefs gathered in force at Zhiheji and came to terms with the Taiping armies, Zhang Lexing was granted a noble title, and for a time the Nian were placed inside the Taiping system of northern expeditions and western campaigns as a mobile force in the north. After the fall of the Taiping the Nian broke away completely and became an independent armed power in the north, and during the 1860s they held wide stretches of country along the borders of northern Anhui, northern Jiangsu, eastern Henan and western Shandong. The other side was the Qing court and its regional forces: the centre worked through the Grand Council and the Ministry of Revenue to assign money, and the war zone was divided among the Governor-General of the Huai River, the Governor-General of the Liangguang, the Governor-General of Zhili and the provincial governors of Henan, Shandong and Anhui. Green Standard and banner troops held towns, militias and drill corps held the countryside, and brave units did the attacking. From 1855 the Mongol cavalry of Sengge Rinchen, drawn from Chahar, became the main pursuing force; from the 1860s the Chu and Huai armies of Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang, equipped with foreign muskets and rifled guns bought in Shanghai, became the arm of assault, and Li Hongzhang moved grain and munitions along the Grand Canal in grain boats. Local militias, village forts and labour gangs formed the depth of the Qing line, while the grain depots and the canal transport along the Grand Canal were the lifeline of its supply. The line between the two camps was not simply one of rulers and ruled: most of the Nian were peasants, canal boatmen and refugees pressed into service, assessed for recruits, grain and taxes, and as the war went on local militia bands and scattered troops repeatedly changed flags and went over to the Nian side.
people: 捻軍最重要的首領是安徽亳州人張樂行。他出身貧寒，早年在皖北聚眾結社，一八五一年在蒙城起義，一八五二年攻入雉河集，以捻首之首自居，一八五三年受太平天國封爵並與之合流；一八五五年在安徽亳州三河集一帶與湘軍鮑超所部及僧格林沁的蒙古騎兵交戰中陣亡。他的死使捻軍第一次失去共同的旗主，各股自此分立，號令不齊，成敗更繫於個別首領的膽量與運氣。其後主持大股的是族姪張宗禹，此人久與清軍追剿周旋，善用騎兵流竄，在太平天國覆亡後成為捻軍事實上的核心，他於一八六八年被清軍擊敗於山東高唐一帶，北走塞外而亡。張樂行的弟弟亦統率一部，於一八六八年在安徽陣亡，至此捻軍大股盡散。魯西黑旗首領宋景詩一度在清與捻之間起伏，一八六三年在魯西攻戰中陣亡。太平天國方面與捻軍直接相關者是陳玉成與李秀成：陳玉成在太平軍西征中率部北上，於三河集一役吃緊之際得李秀成自滁州馳援之兵解圍，其後奉命同捻軍會師亳州，把捻軍正式編入太平軍的北伐序列。清方可用之人更多：袁甲三以河南巡撫身分主持豫東剿捻，江忠源率楚勇入皖、兵敗於壽州，曾國藩坐鎮兩江、以練勇與結壘之法對付流動之敵，李鴻章接手淮軍與蘇北軍務；一八五五年起有僧格林沁以蒙古騎兵追擊，一八六五年病逝軍中，一八六六年由馮子材接手畿輔剿捻，丁寶楨以山東巡撫身分在魯西部署，劉銘傳、張樹聲、吳長慶等淮軍將領則負責攻寨與封鎖線的實際作戰。
peopleEn: The most important leader of the Nian was Zhang Lexing, a native of Bozhou in Anhui. He came from poor stock and had gathered followers in northern Anhui for years; he rose at Mengcheng in 1851 and took Zhiheji in 1852, where he established himself as the chief of the Nian, and in 1853 he was granted a title by the Taiping and moved over to their side; in 1855 he was killed in the fighting near Sanheji in Bozhou against the troops of the Xiang commander Bao Chao and the Mongol cavalry of Sengge Rinchen. His death left the Nian for the first time without a common banner leader: the separate banners went their own ways from that point on, orders were no longer uniform, and success depended more on the nerve and luck of individual chiefs. The great band was afterwards led by his clan nephew Zhang Zongyu, who long evaded the Qing columns, used his mounted men to shift constantly and, after the fall of the Taiping, became the effective core of the movement; he was defeated by the Qing around Gaotang in Shandong in 1868 and died after fleeing north beyond the frontier. Zhang Lexing's brother led another band and was killed in Anhui in the same year, and with him the great Nian formations dissolved. In western Shandong the Black Flag leader Song Jingshi moved back and forth between the Qing and the Nian before being killed in action there in 1863. On the Taiping side the two men directly connected with the Nian were Chen Yucheng and Li Xiucheng: Chen Yucheng led his troops north during the western campaign, and when his position at Sanheji became critical he was relieved by a force brought up by Li Xiucheng from Chuzhou, after which he was ordered to join the Nian at Bozhou and to place the Nian formally in the Taiping northern expedition series. The Qing had many more usable men: Yuan Sansan directed the suppression in eastern Henan as governor of that province, Jiang Zhongyuan led the Chu braves into Anhui and was defeated at Shouzhou, Zeng Guofan sat at Nanjing and met a mobile enemy with drilled troops and a policy of entrenching, and Li Hongzhang took over the Huai army and the operations in northern Jiangsu. From 1855 the pursuit was led by Sengge Rinchen with his Mongol cavalry; he died of illness in camp in 1865, and in 1866 Feng Zicai took over the suppression in the capital region. Ding Baozhen, governor of Shandong, deployed in western Shandong, and Huai commanders such as Liu Mingchuan, Zhang Shusheng and Wu Changqing were responsible for the practical work of storming the forts and holding the blockade lines.
kits: 本卡線膛砲是清方在剿捻中最終壓過捻軍的關鍵技術之一。線膛砲以膛線賦予彈丸旋轉，使同樣藥量的射程遠於舊式滑膛炮，精度亦更高，代價是必須使用專配藥包、整裝發射速度慢、重量與價格都遠高於抬炮，一門野戰砲往往需要數十人拖曳；就一八五〇年代的歐洲而言，它已是新興技術，到一八六〇年代才隨上海的軍火交易與江南製造總局、蘇州洋炮局的仿製，逐步裝備到清軍手上。清廷在一八六〇年代中期把它投入剿捻，最先用於攻擊捻軍圩寨：線膛砲在外圍一二百步外精確射擊寨牆上的人頭與槍眼，使守寨者無法抬頭，再由步槍與抬槍掩護工兵掘壕、架雲梯，最後步兵突入。捻軍幾乎沒有同類火力，其所有火炮多為從太平軍繳獲的抬炮與舊式滑膛炮，口徑大、射程短、精度低，只能在近距離平射寨門，遇上遠程精確射擊幾乎沒有還手之力，這正是兩者在火力上的分野。捻軍本身的主流兵器是冷兵器，大刀、長矛、叉、標槍，配合鳥槍與少量從太平軍繳獲的抬槍；騎兵是其真正的力量所在，馬匹多自河南、山東農村徵集，每騎攜帶足供數日馳騁的乾糧與繩索，以便隨時拆營轉移。官軍方面除線膛砲外，還有綠營與團練使用的抬槍與鳥槍、八旗與蒙古騎兵配備的馬槍與佩刀，淮軍則大量裝備洋式步槍，並以線膛砲與抬槍組成攻寨火力。攻城器械方面，雙方都用雲梯、攻門槌、濠溝與木柵；運輸則以運河漕船為主，北方尚無可供大軍使用的鐵路，糧食、彈藥、攻城砲與重車全靠水陸轉運，這條漕運線在往後的封鎖戰中成為清軍戰略的支點。
kitsEn: The rifled field gun on this card was one of the key technologies that eventually let the Qing overmatch the Nian. Rifling gives the shot its rotation, so the same charge of powder carries much further than in an old smooth-bore gun and the accuracy is better; the price is that the piece needs its own prepared ammunition, fires slowly, and is far heavier and dearer than a field swivel, with a single field gun often needing several score of men to drag it. For the 1850s in Europe it was still a new technology, and it was only in the 1860s, through military purchases in Shanghai and through the imitations of the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Suzhou arsenal, that it began to reach the Qing army. The court put it into the war against the Nian from the mid-1860s, first of all to attack the Nian stockades: the rifled gun fired accurate shots at the heads and firing slits along the ramparts from a hundred or two hundred paces outside, keeping the defenders pinned down, while muskets and swivel guns covered the sappers as they dug in and set up ladders and the infantry went over the top. The Nian had almost nothing comparable. All their guns were swivel pieces and old smooth-bores captured from the Taiping: large calibre, short range, poor accuracy, useful only to shoot level at the gate of a fort, and with hardly any answer to accurate fire at long range. That was the divide in artillery between the two sides. The main weapons of the Nian were cold arms, broadswords, spears, pitchforks and javelins, with hunting guns and a few swivel pieces taken from the Taiping. Their real strength was the horse: the animals were levied from the villages of Henan and Shandong, and each rider carried enough dry food and rope for several days in the saddle so that the column could break camp and shift at any moment. On the Qing side, besides the rifled guns, the Green Standard and the militias used swivel guns and matchlocks, the banner troops and the Mongol cavalry carried carbines and sabres, and the Huai armies were largely equipped with foreign muskets, with rifled guns and swivels forming the artillery of assault. For siege work both sides used ladders, battering rams, ditches and wooden stockades. Movement was by canal boat above all, for the north had no railway yet available to a field army: grain, ammunition, heavy guns and all the wagons of the train went by water and road, and that canal line became the hinge of Qing strategy in the blockade that followed.
tactics: 捻軍的戰術核心是流動。捻眾多不據城而據村，築圩寨自守，遇官軍大隊則避走，避實擊虛、不與決戰；游擊多以馬隊出奇不意地插入官軍縱隊側後，焚其糧車、襲其營寨，旋即遠颺，故清方屢有剿而不能滅之嘆。圩寨是捻軍防守的基本形式，土牆高厚、外壕深闊、寨門狹窄並設拒馬，寨內屯糧、蓄水、繫馬，能擋騎兵衝鋒而不便官軍以雲梯攀緣；攻取州縣則靠挖地道、焚城門與雲梯突進，常在攻堅中折於城下。地形是捻軍的盟友：黃河下游屢改道、豫東與蘇北的運河水網、魯西的鹽鹼地與沼澤，使追擊的騎兵屢屢失速，捻軍便可乘隙重整。作戰紀律上，老捻精於騎射與游擊，新捻則多為附眾，器械與組織都較粗鬆，一旦失利便易潰散。清軍的戰術在十七年裡換了兩次。第一次是曾國藩式的練勇與結壘：築壘紮營、不求速勝、以穩制躁，用火槍齊射與短程砲火支援冷兵器衝鋒，並靠糧臺與漕船維持遠距離作戰所需的糧秣；僧格林沁接手後改以蒙古騎兵窮追猛打，利用追擊消耗捻軍的馬匹與體力，確實在皖北、豫東屢奏功，但其縱隊糧秣拖累太重，馬力難繼，捻軍只要退回村落便能重新站起。第二次轉變發生在一八六六年之後：馮子材接手畿輔剿捻，改追剿為堵剿，在直隸與山東交界沿運河與驛道修築連續的壕溝與木牆，分設糧臺與卡壘，把捻軍活動範圍逐步壓縮到魯西、豫東一帶的有限地帶，再集中兵力攻寨，攻堅時以線膛砲與洋槍在遠程壓制寨牆，步槍齊射掩護工兵掘壕架梯，突入之後再以騎兵追擊潰散之眾。一八六八年山東高唐一役是這一套辦法的結果：捻軍因跑不出封鎖線而在寨中被攻破，張宗禹僅率少數人北走。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of the Nian was movement. The Nian did not hold cities so much as villages, building earthen forts to sit in; when a Qing column came they withdrew, avoiding the strong and striking the weak, and refused a set-piece battle. Their raids were mounted parties that fell unexpectedly on the flank and rear of a Qing column, burned the grain carts, hit the camps and were gone again, which is why the Qing so often found they could hunt the Nian down but not destroy them. The earthen fort was the basic form of Nian defence: thick walls, a broad outer ditch, a narrow gate protected by a chevaux-de-frise, with grain, water and tethered horses inside. It could stop a cavalry charge and made it awkward for the assaulting party to mount a ladder, and it was the taking of walled towns that usually cost the Nian dearly, for they attacked with saps, fire against the gates and ladders, and were often broken against the walls. The country was the Nian ally: the lower Yellow River had shifted its course repeatedly, the canal network of eastern Henan and northern Jiangsu and the salt flats and marshes of western Shandong slowed the pursuing cavalry and gave the Nian time to reform. In discipline, the old Nian were skilled with the lance and the horse, while many of the new Nian were followers with poor kit and loose organisation who broke at the first reverse. The Qing changed their method twice in the seventeen years of the war. The first was Zeng Guofan drilled volunteers and entrenched camps: build the camp, take no risks, wear the enemy down, fire volleys of musket covered by short-range guns against the cold-armed assault, and keep the grain depots and the canal boats going so that an army fighting far from home could be fed. When Sengge Rinchen took over he switched to pursuit with Mongol cavalry, spending the Nian horses and bodies of men in the chase, and this won him real successes in northern Anhui and eastern Henan; but his columns were badly burdened with supplies, the horses could not keep the pace, and once the Nian could slip back into a village they were on their feet again. The second change came after 1866, when Feng Zicai took over the suppression in the capital region. He replaced pursuit with blockade, ran a continuous ditch and wooden wall along the canal and the post roads on the border of Zhili and Shandong, established grain depots and stockades at intervals, and squeezed the area of Nian movement down to the limited ground of western Shandong and eastern Henan, then concentrated troops against the forts. The artillery method was to use rifled guns and foreign muskets at long range to pin the ramparts, cover the sappers with musket volleys while they dug and set ladders, and then send the cavalry after the men who broke out. The action at Gaotang in Shandong in 1868 was the result of that whole method: the Nian, unable to run past the blockade line, were stormed in their forts, and Zhang Zongyu escaped north with a handful of men.
data: 可核對的數字與時間如下。捻軍起義自一八五一年起，至一八六八年夏被平定，前後約十七年；一八五一年張樂行於蒙城起義，一八五二年取雉河集，一八五三年太平天國定都南京後兩軍互聯，同年清廷起用蒙古騎兵追擊捻軍，一八五五年張樂行在亳州三河集陣亡。一八六〇年太平軍攻取蘇州，一八六三年十二月蘇州為淮軍所陷，一八六四年七月天京陷落，捻軍此後失去倚仗，全線獨撐。一八六五年四月，僧格林沁在安徽亳州高樓寨攻破捻軍大寨，捻軍騎兵損失以數千計；同年四月捻軍在河北吳橋一帶設伏反擊，僧格林沁所部步騎損失數千，僧格林沁本人重傷退回濟南，五月病逝軍中。一八六六年清廷以馮子材接手直隸、山東剿捻，他沿兩省交界修築壕溝與木牆，連續長達數百里；一八六七年淮軍劉銘傳等部在魯西、豫東攻破捻軍多處大寨，捻軍兵力自此折損過半。一八六八年捻軍在山東高唐一帶被擊敗，張宗禹北走塞外，張樂行之弟於同年死在安徽，捻軍至夏末基本平定。兵力方面，捻軍在極盛時的數目各方記載出入甚大，常被誇大為百萬之眾，較為可靠的說法是十餘萬至數十萬不等；僧格林沁所部蒙古騎兵為萬餘之眾，淮軍與勇營投入剿捻的兵力在數萬以上，而清廷每年用於剿捻的軍費以數千萬兩計，成為晚清財政的重大負擔。
dataEn: The figures and dates that can be checked run as follows. The rising began in 1851 and was put down in the summer of 1868, about seventeen years in all. Zhang Lexing rose at Mengcheng in 1851 and took Zhiheji in 1852; after the Taiping settled at Nanjing in 1853 the two movements came to terms; the court began using the Mongol cavalry against the Nian in the same year, and in 1855 Zhang Lexing was killed at Sanheji in Bozhou. The Taiping took Suzhou in 1860, Suzhou fell to the Huai army in December 1863, and Nanjing fell in July 1864, after which the Nian lost their support and stood alone. In April 1865 Sengge Rinchen stormed a great Nian stockade at Gaolouzhai near Bozhou, where the Nian lost several thousand horses and riders; in the same month the Nian ambushed him at Wuzhao in Zhili, inflicting several thousand losses on his infantry and cavalry, and Sengge Rinchen, badly wounded, was carried back to Jinan and died in May. In 1866 the court put Feng Zicai in charge of the suppression in Zhili and Shandong, and he began running the ditch and wooden wall along the frontier, a continuous work of several hundred li. In 1867 Huai commanders such as Liu Mingchuan broke Nian strongholds in western Shandong and eastern Henan, and the Nian strength was more than halved. In 1868 they were beaten at Gaotang in Shandong; Zhang Zongyu fled north beyond the frontier, Zhang Lexing's brother was killed in Anhui in the same year, and by the end of the summer the movement was over. On numbers: the size of the Nian at their height is recorded very differently by different sources and is often inflated to a million, whereas a more defensible figure is somewhere between a hundred thousand and several hundred thousand; the Mongol cavalry of Sengge Rinchen numbered something over ten thousand; the Huai army and the drill corps committed to the suppression ran into the tens of thousands; and the court was spending millions of taels a year on the war, a heavy charge on late Qing finances.
cause: 捻軍起義的直接起因，是太平天國起義撕開了清廷在中原的防線。咸豐元年太平軍在廣西金田起義，所過州縣望風瓦解，直隸、河南、山東、安徽一帶的地方團練倉促組建，兵源不精、操練未熟、糧餉無著，為數年之後的捻軍興起留下大片空白。社會層面，黃河下游連年水患與災荒使豫東、皖北、蘇北人口流失、游民成群，運河沿線的船丁、鹽丁與失地農民構成廣大的武裝人力池；清廷在戰事中攤派丁、糧、稅，催科之下逼反，反复把民眾推向武裝。另一層原因是教門的傳播：白蓮教支派在皖北、豫東的民間長期留存，捻黨承其餘緒，兼具互助與抗稅的色彩。捻黨本身並非一八五一年突然出現，它在河南、山東、安徽一帶以捻為名，捻在豫皖方言中指聚攏、捏合成團，數十年間靠開壇、聚眾、練拳棒與互助掩護維持組織。爆發的導火線有三：一是清廷把主力東調對付太平軍，皖北與豫東兵力空虛；二是咸豐元年至三年連續的旱澇與糧荒，饑民大批流入皖北；三是團練與官軍在徵糧、緝捕上手段峻烈，把原本零散的抗稅聚眾推向與官府直接對抗。一八五一年張樂行在蒙城起義、一八五二年攻入雉河集建立基地，即在此背景下成形；一八五三年太平天國定都南京，捻軍看到了北方的機會，遂在雉河集大集各旗與之合流，把一場地方性的抗稅暴動推成跨省的長期戰爭。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the Nian rising was the gap torn in the Qing defences of the central plains by the Taiping rebellion. When the Taiping rose at Jintian in Guangxi in the first year of Xianfeng the prefectures and counties along their path collapsed without a fight, and the local militias in Zhili, Henan, Shandong and Anhui were raised in haste, with unreliable men, untrained soldiers and no money to feed them, leaving a large empty space that the Nian would fill a few years later. At the social level, repeated floods and famine on the lower Yellow River displaced populations across eastern Henan, northern Anhui and northern Jiangsu and threw up large pools of vagrants, while the boatmen, salt workers and landless peasants of the canal regions supplied the manpower for an armed movement; the levies of men, grain and tax demanded by the court in time of war, and the harsh collection methods that went with them, repeatedly pushed people towards armed resistance. A second cause lay in the spread of the sects: branches of the White Lotus persisted among the people of northern Anhui and eastern Henan for a long time, and the Nian societies carried on that inheritance while at the same time carrying a character of mutual aid and tax resistance. The Nian societies did not appear suddenly in 1851. In Henan, Shandong and Anhui they had been known for decades under the name Nian, a word of the Henan and Anhui dialect meaning to gather or press into a mass, and they had kept themselves alive through covenant meetings, massing of followers, practice of fists and sticks, and mutual protection. Three things triggered the outbreak: the court drew its main strength east against the Taiping and left northern Anhui and eastern Henan thinly held; drought and flood and a bad harvest in the first three years of Xianfeng drove hungry people into northern Anhui in thousands; and the militia and the regulars, harsh in the levying of grain and in the hunting of suspects, pushed scattered bands of tax resisters into open confrontation with the authorities. The rising of Zhang Lexing at Mengcheng in 1851 and the taking of Zhiheji in 1852 to serve as a base were formed in that setting; and when the Taiping settled at Nanjing in 1853 the Nian saw their chance in the north, gathered their banners in force at Zhiheji and joined the Taiping, turning what had been a local revolt against taxation into a long war across several provinces.
impact: 捻軍起義對清廷的衝擊，首先是軍事體制的重整。此戰顯示綠營與旗營已無力應付以騎兵為骨幹的流動敵患，團練與勇營遂由臨時應急變為長期編制，湘軍與淮軍自此成為清朝的野戰主力；蒙古騎兵在剿捻中嶄露頭角，卻也暴露追擊式騎兵戰爭的極限，僧格林沁死後蒙騎逐步裁汰。技術上，一八六〇年代清廷加快近代火砲引進與自製，江南製造總局於一八六五年建成，天津機器局與福州船政局相繼設立，線膛砲與洋槍成為勇營的標準配備，剿捻的實戰需求正是這一輪洋務起步的直接推力之一。財政上，十七年的剿捻軍費以數千萬兩計，疊加太平天國的軍費開支，使清廷更依賴厘金與加派，財政積弊更深。在戰術與制度層面，馮子材改追剿為堵剿、修築壕溝長城、設糧臺卡壘的辦法，後來成為清廷對付西北回亂與太平餘部的基本方略；結壘紮穩、以靜制動等主張也在清軍戰術文獻中留下痕跡。地方社會層面，皖北、蘇北、豫東一帶因長期戰亂而村莊堡壘化，練勇與寨團成為鄉村自衛的常態，此後地方武力與國家軍隊互相滲透。捻軍自身的失敗也留下教訓：各股缺乏統一旗主與統一政權，沒有可持續的後方與稅收，兵源流動而忠誠不齊，缺砲兵與攻城能力，故攻城多敗、流動有餘而據守無力；這些經驗在太平天國與捻軍先後失敗之後，被清廷與後世軍人視為近代化裝備與集中指揮的重要理由。
impactEn: The shock of the Nian rising to the Qing court was first of all a reorganisation of the military system. The war showed that the Green Standard and the banner troops were no longer equal to a mobile enemy whose backbone was cavalry, and the militia and the drill corps changed from improvised measures of emergency into permanent establishments; the Xiang and Huai armies from that point on were the field army of the dynasty. Mongol cavalry made their name in the war against the Nian, but the campaign also showed the limits of pursuit by horse, and after the death of Sengge Rinchen the Mongol horse was gradually disbanded. On the technical side, the court hurried the introduction and the domestic production of modern artillery during the 1860s: the Jiangnan Arsenal was completed in 1865, the Tientsin arsenal and the Foochow shipyard followed, and rifled guns and foreign muskets became the standard equipment of the drill corps, with the practical demands of the war against the Nian one of the direct pushes behind that first phase of the self-strengthening movement. Financially, seventeen years of campaigning against the Nian cost millions of taels a year, on top of the war against the Taiping, and forced the court further onto likin and surtaxes, deepening the fiscal rot. At the level of tactics and institutions, the change Feng Zicai made from pursuit to blockade, with his ditches and walls, his grain depots and his stockaded lines, became the standard method of the Qing against the Muslim rising in the north-west and the surviving Taiping forces; the doctrines of entrenching, holding firm and letting the enemy come became part of the tactical writing of the Qing army. In the local society of northern Anhui, northern Jiangsu and eastern Henan, long war turned villages into forts, and drill corps and village bands became the normal way a village defended itself, so that local military power and the armies of the state grew into each other afterwards. The defeat of the Nian left lessons of its own: the banners had no common leader and no common state, no lasting rear area and no revenue of their own, the ranks were fluid and the loyalty uneven, and without artillery or siege capacity they won nothing against walled towns and held nothing but their mobility. After the failures of both the Taiping and the Nian, these lessons were read by the Qing and by later soldiers as arguments for modern equipment and centralised command.
result: 一八六八年夏，捻軍在清軍的封鎖與攻堅中被完全平定。張宗禹於山東高唐一帶被馮子材的淮軍擊敗，僅率數百人北走，越過山海關外，據各方記載終於在張家口以西的草原上兵敗身亡；張樂行之弟於同年死在安徽，餘部或散或降，魯西黑旗等附眾亦先後被清剿。綿延十七年、橫跨四省邊界的捻軍起義至此結束。清廷以慘重的代價換來這場平定。僧格林沁在吳橋一役重傷退回濟南，五月即病逝軍中，蒙古騎兵追擊路線的失敗暴露在朝野面前；淮軍與地方練勇在戰後迅速膨脹，成為晚清地方武力的主力，而以團練、練勇、寨堡編織的鄉村防禦體系在豫、皖、蘇北長期延續，國家軍隊與地方武力的界線從此模糊。從兵器與戰術的意義看，這是一場流動騎兵對上集中火力的較量。線膛砲代表的精確遠程火砲，在攻寨時把守軍壓在土牆之內，使冷兵器與鳥槍為主的守軍難以還手；捻軍既不能取得同等的火力，就只能不據城、不守野，長期流動，最終仍被封鎖線與攻堅的節奏夾住。清代剿捻史由此得出一條結論：對付以騎兵為骨幹、靠速度維生的武裝，光靠追擊並不夠，必須同時具備封鎖、固定，以及足以壓制寨牆的遠程火力。捻軍起義的敗亡，也為其後洋槍與新式砲兵主導的近代化戰爭鋪了路。
resultEn: In the summer of 1868 the Nian were finally put down, between the Qing blockade and the Qing assault. Zhang Zongyu was beaten by the Huai troops of Feng Zicai around Gaotang in Shandong and escaped north with a few hundred men; he passed beyond Shanhaiguan and, according to the several accounts that survive, was brought down and lost on the grasslands west of Zhangjiakou. Zhang Lexing's brother was killed in Anhui in the same year, the remnants scattered or came in, and the Black Flag and other attached bands in western Shandong were cleared away in turn. A rising that had run for seventeen years across the borders of four provinces came to an end. The Qing paid heavily for that victory. Sengge Rinchen was badly wounded at Wuzhao, was carried back to Jinan and died of illness within weeks, and the failure of his line of pursuit was laid bare before the court. The Huai army and the local drill corps expanded quickly after the war and became the main military force of the late Qing, while the system of militia, drill corps and village forts lasted for a long time in Henan, Anhui and northern Jiangsu, blurring the line between the armies of the state and the armed strength of the localities. In terms of arms and tactics this was a trial of mobile cavalry against concentrated firepower. The rifled gun stood for accurate artillery at long range, which pinned the defenders behind their earthen walls and left an enemy armed with cold arms and matchlocks with little way to answer. Unable to obtain artillery of its own, the Nian could not hold cities or hold the field; they could only keep moving, and were finally closed in between the blockade line and the rhythm of the assault. The history of the Qing war against the Nian thus yielded a single conclusion: against an armed force whose backbone was cavalry and whose life depended on speed, pursuit alone was not enough; one had to combine blockade, fixity, and long-range firepower strong enough to beat down a rampart. The fall of the Nian cleared the way for the later age of foreign muskets and modern artillery.
